title: A Wolf for the Ember
premise: Wendell Okafor, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has hidden her magic for fifteen years in Grayhollow, a city that outlawed it after the Sundering. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Wendell learns the covenant binding the living world to the spirit realm is failing—and the child is its last living anchor. Hunted by the Inquisitor's Wardens and betrayed by an old lover now serving the law, Wendell must gather the scattered Ember Stones and reforge the covenant at the Hollow Gate before the dead spill into the living world. She succeeds only by surrendering her own memories of everyone she loves, choosing justice and duty over the self she has built—though the final chapter hints the child remembers her still.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in Eastern European village churches before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about grief, memory, and the small magics people practice to survive.

chapters.title: The Knocker of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her shop in Grayhollow: charms carved from animal bone, each whispering faintly to her. She hides her gift behind mundane craft, paying quiet bribes to stay unregistered. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as safety, established through her ritual of silencing the bones each night.

chapters.title: A Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A girl of perhaps eight appears at her door during a curfew storm, speaking a language that makes the dead-bones sing in answer. The child cannot or will not speak Common. Wendell takes her in against every instinct. Beat: fear warring with recognition—the language sounds like her grandmother's lullabies.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Warden patrols sweep the district after reports of 'unlicensed resonance.' Wendell hides the child, Sefa, and learns from a frightened neighbor that three hedge-witches were taken this week. Beat: the cost of invisibility—she once watched a friend burn and did nothing.

chapters.title: The Language Under Language
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, rendered as impressionistic fragments she half-understands. She fled something called the Hollow Gate; the words she speaks are covenant-speech, and they are dying from the world. Beat: a child carrying an inheritance too heavy for her shoulders.

chapters.title: An Old Flame in a Gray Coat
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inquisitor Mara Voss—Wendell's first love, fifteen years estranged—arrives at the shop on inspection, courteous and lethal. Their charged exchange reveals Mara suspects but hasn't proof. Beat: old love sharpened into mutual danger; duty has remade her.

chapters.title: The First Ember Stone
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following the bones' song, Wendell retrieves an Ember Stone sewn inside a hanged witch's burial shroud, communing briefly with the woman's angry ghost. Beat: grief and guilt—the ghost knew her grandmother, and blames the Okafor line for the covenant's fracture.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Bone Market
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She seeks the smuggler Osric, who moves magical goods beneath the city. He agrees to help—for a price: her silence about his operation, and a carving of his drowned daughter so he can hear her once. Beat: compassion weaponized; Wendell sees her own temptation mirrored.

chapters.title: Sefa Speaks
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Through shared dreams, Sefa shows Wendell the Sundering: how the founders broke the covenant to seize power, scattering the Ember Stones, cursing the gatekeepers' line—Wendell's line. Beat: revelation reframes everything; Wendell's exile was engineered.

chapters.title: The Warden's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds evidence of Wendell's magic and sits with the warrant all night, remembering who Wendell was before the purges. She files a partial report, omitting the child. Beat: love against duty begins tearing her in two.

chapters.title: The Second Stone and the Price of Hearing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The second stone lies in a plague-pit beneath the Inquisitors' Hall. Wendell infiltrates during a memorial service, guided by the pit's thousands of dead. Beat: horror and awe; the dead do not want rescue—they want witness, and Wendell promises it.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bone Market
chapters.summary: Osric's POV. Pressured by Wardens holding his son, Osric gives up Wendell's route. He tells himself the trade is mercy. Beat: complicity and self-deception; even good men feed the machine.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Undervault
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell/Sefa POV. Wardens raid the shop; Wendell and Sefa flee into the undervaults with the two stones, pursued by hounds that smell magic. They escape through Osric's secret passage—he looks away deliberately, half-redemption. Beat: terror, trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Ashfen
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Outside the city they find Mother Ilya, a exiled gatekeeper who trained Wendell's grandmother. Ilya teaches Sefa's role as anchor and Wendell's as reforging hand—and warns the third stone lies beyond the Veil itself. Beat: reluctant apprenticeship; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Mara Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her omissions discovered, Mara is given a choice: capture Wendell or be purged alongside her. She requests the hunt herself. Beat: duty hardening into armor over a cracking heart.

chapters.title: The Third Stone Beyond the Veil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At a thin place in Ashfen marshes, Wendell crosses into the spirit realm, bartering memories—one year of them per step—to reach the stone guarded by her grandmother's shade. Beat: sacrifice begins; memory as currency, foreshadowing the ending.

chapters.title: The Dead Give Testimony
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Sefa's POV. The spirits gather to judge whether the covenant deserves reforging, since it was built on the founders' theft. Wendell argues not for restoration but for a new covenant—justice outside the old law. Beat: thematic climax of argument; the dead are moved but demand a price.

chapters.title: Ashfen Burns
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wardens track them to Ashfen. Ilya dies holding the pass, buying time; Sefa is captured by Mara's squad. Wendell, wounded, holds three stones that sing toward the fourth—held in the Inquisitors' vault. Beat: devastating loss; rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Women at the Vault Door
chapters.summary: Mara and Wendell, alternating POV. Mara confronts Wendell at the Hall; instead of arresting her, Mara opens the vault—choosing love and justice over the institution that owns her. Beat: the romance's fulcrum; Mara accepts ruin.

chapters.title: March on the Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. With Mara's help Wendell frees Sefa, seizes the fourth stone, and leads a procession of the city's hidden faithful to the Hollow Gate as the veil visibly thins—shadows walking, ancestors pressing through. Beat: rising crescendo; the invisible made visible at last.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, Wendell's POV. At the Gate, the price is named: a life's worth of memory to bind the new covenant. Wendell carves the stones into a single ember, speaks the old language Sefa taught her, and lets go—her mother's face, her years with Mara, her own name dissolving. Beat: love against duty resolved through ultimate sacrifice.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mara's POV. The covenant holds; magic is decriminalized by a shaken council. Mara tends a Wendell who no longer knows her, keeping the shop open, telling her their story nightly like a charm. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; love persisting without recognition.

chapters.title: Ember, Remembered
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sefa's POV, one year later. Sefa, now apprentice gatekeeper, discovers that covenant-magic preserves what it consumes: within the ember's warmth, Wendell's memories sleep. She begins teaching them back to her, one lullaby at a time. Final beat: memory endures; the smallest voice carries the oldest promise.
